text:
Your vault is encrypted on your own device before anything is sent to our servers. When you enter your master password, the app runs it through PBKDF2, a key-derivation function, 600,000 times to create your encryption key. The repetition is deliberate. It makes every password guess slow and costly, so anyone trying to brute-force your master password has to do a huge amount of work for each attempt.

That key then encrypts your vault with AES-256, one of the most widely trusted encryption standards in the world. Without the correct key, the encrypted data can't be read.

Our servers never see your master password. They store only your encrypted vault, which looks like random noise to anyone who doesn't have your key, including us. Even if our servers were breached, attackers would get only scrambled data they couldn't read.

This also means your master password is the one thing that unlocks your vault. Make it long and unique, and keep it to yourself. Because we never see it, protecting it is up to you.
